card.name: Word 'no' opening overdosage statements
card.fires_on: Mostly the word 'no' right after 'There is' at the start of an OVERDOSAGE section, as in 'no known antidote'. It also fires weakly on other linking words in label sentences, such as 'have', 'which' and 'occur'.

modes.label: No-treatment opener
modes.description: The word 'no' after 'There is' or 'There is currently' at the start of an overdosage section.
modes.example: 10 OVERDOSAGE There is<< no>> known specific treatment for overdose with JULU

modes.label: Linking words in warnings
modes.description: Words like 'have', 'which' or 'occur' that continue a clause in interaction or risk sentences.
modes.example: Use caution when administering imatinib mesylate tablets with CYP2D6 substrates that<< have>> a narrow therapeutic window.

card.writes: Its promoted and suppressed tokens look unrelated (code and Chinese literature words versus science words), so the output effect is unclear.
card.plain: It lights up on the word 'no' when an overdosage section says there is no known treatment or information.
